photo.label: Photo (DINOv2-L)
photo.note: Frozen self-supervised ViT on the raw photograph; strongest image retrieval but carries museum photography signatures.

silhouette.label: Silhouette (DINOv2-B)
silhouette.note: Background and texture removed; pure 2-D outline. Weakest museum signature.

adapted.label: Adapted (photo-randomised)
adapted.note: DINOv2-B partially fine-tuned on train-split groups against catalog text with background/resolution randomisation.

ends.label: Working ends
ends.note: Best-matching pair of the two terminal 30% crops (orientation-aligned).

multimodal.label: Multimodal
multimodal.note: Equal mean of photo, silhouette and multilingual catalog-text cosines over records with all three.

limitations: Targets are weak catalog-derived categories and rule-based function labels; no expert-reviewed ground truth exists.
Text representations are circular with respect to these targets and are shown only as consistency checks.
Raw-photo embeddings carry museum photography signatures (background, resolution); silhouettes reduce them but lose internal detail.
Images are mostly 120-320 px catalog thumbnails; working ends of thin instruments are often unresolved.
Similarity is not ancestry: neighbours show similar 2-D form, shared mechanism or shared photography, not historical descent.
Calibrated agreement values estimate agreement with existing rules on held-out groups, not the probability of actual use.
Adapted models were fit on train-split groups with near-duplicate-aware splits; three seeds; small data.
Generated outlines are 2-D form hypotheses from a small diffusion model trained on uncalibrated photographs; they carry no scale, mechanism, material or function and are not designs.
training_performed: bounded adaptation of a pretrained encoder; see adaptation runs; a small text- and date-conditioned silhouette diffusion model trained from scratch (see generate.json)
